Free version, type, income sources, what it submits and CIS come from HMRC's software finder (read 18 November 2026). "CIS on tax return" means HMRC lists the product as ready to report Construction Industry Scheme deductions on your tax return. Prices and joint-property support come from each provider's own website (checked 18 November 2026); "Unknown" means we haven't confirmed it yet. How we check.

Free options we have price-checked

These are free, or have a free plan, according to the provider's own website. Free plans usually have limits, so read the note before you choose.

  • Aligned.tax MTD for Spreadsheets: Free for individuals – Filing your own quarterly updates is free for individuals; accountants pay per client from the 2027/28 tax year.
  • Clear Books Free: Free – Sole Trader Free, Property Free and Foreign Property Free (one property) plans at £0.
  • Coconut Free: Free version (per HMRC) – HMRC lists a free Coconut product; its limits were not checked.
  • FreeAgent for free with Mettle, NatWest & RBS: Free for eligible bank customers – Free while you keep a NatWest, Royal Bank of Scotland or Ulster Bank business current account, or a Mettle account with at least one transaction a month.
  • GetGround: Free (Basic plan) – MTD for landlords free with GetGround's Basic plan.
  • Landlord Studio: Free up to 3 properties + £5 per MTD submission; Pro £12 + VAT/month – MTD Go plan is free for up to 3 properties but charges £5 per MTD tax submission. Pro £12 + VAT/month includes MTD submissions.
  • My Tax Digital (Free): Free – Describes itself as free MTD software for Income Tax and VAT, with a bridging mode that imports spreadsheet figures.
  • Pandle: Free; Pro £5/month + VAT – Free Pandle plan; Pandle Pro £5/month + VAT.
  • PaTMa Property Manager: Free for 1 unit; Pro £15/month – Free plan covers 1 rental unit. Pro £15/month including VAT for 5 units (extra units £1.50/month). 14-day Pro trial.
  • RentalBux Free: Free – Free plan for basic MTD compliance. Joint ownership splits are on paid plans.
  • Sage Sole Trader & Landlord Free: Free – Sole Trader Free: 25 auto-categorised transactions per month, 1 bank account, records landlord income and expenses.
  • TaxPig: Free; Pro £7.50/month – Free Community Edition (£0/month, 50 receipt scans). TaxPig Pro £7.50/month.
  • Zoho: Free plan; paid from £10/month billed annually – Zoho Books Free plan is £0. Its MTD page says sole traders and landlords can manage MTD obligations for free. Standard plan is £10/org/month billed annually (£12 monthly).

Common questions

Does HMRC provide free software for Making Tax Digital?

HMRC's guidance says you, or an agent, will need to use commercial software that works with Making Tax Digital for Income Tax. It also says free products are available for people with simple tax affairs, but they may have limits, such as a set number of transactions. Source: GOV.UK

What is MTD bridging software?

Bridging software connects to records you already keep, such as a spreadsheet, and sends your quarterly updates to HMRC. Some bridging products also submit your tax return; others only send the updates. Use the 'Bridging (spreadsheets)' filter above to see them, or read our guide to spreadsheets and bridging software.

Can I use more than one MTD product?

Yes. HMRC says you can use more than one product, but only one product for each separate submission. For example, a landlord cannot use two products to send the same property quarterly update. If you combine products, make sure together they cover your quarterly updates and your tax return. Source: GOV.UK

When are MTD quarterly updates due?

For both standard and calendar update periods, the deadlines are 7 August, 7 November, 7 February and 7 May (the following tax year). Source: GOV.UK. For what happens if one is late, see MTD penalty points explained. For how the two period types differ, see standard vs calendar update periods.

Does HMRC recommend any MTD software?

No. HMRC says it does not recommend any product or software provider. Every product in this directory has been through HMRC's recognition process, and we show them in alphabetical order by default.

Why does a product say 'Quarterly updates only'?

HMRC lists some products as able to send quarterly updates but not to submit your tax return. If you pick one of those, you'll need another product, or an agent, for the tax return after the year ends.
